description.narrative: Going Global Partnerships is one of the Global Programmes through which the British Council delivers its grant-funded activity. The primary focus of this Global Programme is ODA eligible activity and outcomes. Going Global Partnerships builds strategic, mutually beneficial partnerships in tertiary education between the UK and other countries. These contribute to stronger, more inclusive and globally connected tertiary systems, with the UK seen as a trusted partner. The programme supports partnerships between universities, colleges, education policy makers, civil society organisations and industry partners in the UK and around the world. By building stronger international connections, Going Global Partnerships strengthens higher education and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) systems, enables research collaboration, internationalises institutions, enhances student outcomes and supports inclusion. The majority of the programme is ODA. The countries will benefit through a set of tailored interventions that primarily meet their needs. Going Global Partnerships is defined at a global level but responds to local demand and context through each country undertaking a robust system needs analysis. The scoping process involves a problem-driven approach to determine which partnership interventions and activities can best address local needs. The global programme provides global toolkits, delivery models and standardised processes where relevant, but at a country level, the programme activities are curated to meet local requirements.

ODA counties will develop stronger, more inclusive and globally connected Higher Education (HE) and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) education systems, which support economic and social growth, as the main objective. The change we make:◼Supporting research, knowledge, and innovation collaboration to address local and global challenges and promote inclusive growth.◼Creating an enabling environment, supporting institutions and individuals to benefit from internationalisation.◼Improving the quality, inclusivity and efficiency of higher education and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions and systems.◼Improving the qualities and student outcomes of global graduates (e.g., soft skills, employability).◼Supporting a more equitable and inclusive tertiary education sector.
The audiences for this programme are:◼Education stakeholders.
